info.description:
The Usher Controller's HTTP API.

A bridge calls the token exchange and the revocation channel under a channel assertion. A principal calls the management API, under `/admin`, with an access token from the identity provider. The identity provider's sign-out relay and the health checks carry no credential of their own.

Every refusal from the management API is RFC 9457 problem details, `application/problem+json`, carrying a `code` and repeating no value the request carried. A `2XX` answer is a success of any status from 200 to 299. At the token exchange and the revocation channel, every refusal of one status is identical to every other refusal of that status.

A request schema states only what is refused with `400`: each member's type and the required members. Each operation's `422` names the rules it applies beyond them, and which members it refuses with `422` rather than `400`.

Where an operation says that a principal may see a resource, or may not, it means who may see a resource as `createGrant` defines it.

post.description:
Registers an application and issues its first key, for platform administrators.

The application's `id` is a generated uuid and is its audience: the `aud` carried by its Usher tokens, and the `iss` of its bridge's channel assertions.

`displayName` is stored trimmed and normalized to NFC, the form whose length is counted. `description` is stored trimmed, and a description that is empty once trimmed is stored as `null`. `displayName` is the label shown to people. It is never matched against anything, so two applications may share one.

The key's `value` is in this answer alone. The controller stores it encrypted and never shows it again.

The audit events `application.registration` and then `applicationKey.issuance` record the registration.

A service account receives `serviceAccountNotPermitted`. `noAdministratorYet`: Usher has no administrator yet, and refuses every operation but the first administrator's nomination, its acceptance and a nominee's listing until one accepts.

Revokes one of an application's keys, for platform administrators. Once every controller instance has reloaded its keys, each refuses an exchange or a channel request whose channel assertion is verified only by that key.

The body is sent only with a reason: `rotated`, `compromised` or `retired`.

A key revoked already keeps its first revocation, and a second is refused with `doesNotHold`.

A service account receives `serviceAccountNotPermitted`. `noAdministratorYet`: Usher has no administrator yet, and refuses every operation but the first administrator's nomination, its acceptance and a nominee's listing until one accepts.

422.description: The name is empty, holds a character outside letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, or is not admitted by the payload contract.

2XX.description: The category is registered; `name` carries its scope.

patch.description: Updates a category's description as a JSON Merge Patch, for platform administrators. `null` clears it. The name stays as registered.

A service account receives `serviceAccountNotPermitted`. `noAdministratorYet`: Usher has no administrator yet, and refuses every operation but the first administrator's nomination, its acceptance and a nominee's listing until one accepts.

get.description:
Lists grant requests, a page at a time, in a stable order: those the principal may decide that are pending and have not lapsed, and the principal's own, in any state. An owner of a resource decides the requests on it, and a platform administrator any request but their own.

A request on a retired resource is listed to nobody.

403.description: `serviceAccountNotPermitted`: a service account calls.

422.description: The page size is zero or below it.

post.description:
Grants or refuses a grant request. A request is decided once, by an owner of its resource, as `createGrant` defines one, or by any platform administrator, and never by the principal who asked for it or its holder. To anyone else a request is answered as one that does not exist, as is a request on a retired resource.

Granting a request writes the grant it names, its holder the principal who asked for it, `grantedAt` the instant it is granted and `expiresAt` the request's, with the holder's acceptance showing the capabilities they were shown when they asked, and answers `200` with the `Grant`, `kind` `grant`. A refusal records the decision alone and answers `200` with the decided `GrantRequest`, `kind` `grantRequest`.

A request decided already is refused with `requestDecided`, and one at or past its expiry with `requestLapsed`. Granting a request for a holder holding the grant live already is refused with `alreadyHolds`.

200.description: The request is decided: granted, answered with the grant written, `kind` `grant`; or refused, answered with the request, `kind` `grantRequest`.

403.description: `ownRequest`: the principal asked for the request or is its holder. `serviceAccountNotPermitted`: a service account calls, before any lookup.

404.description: The id is unknown or malformed, names a request on a resource where the principal holds no authority to decide it, or names a request on a retired resource; `requestNotFound` for each.

409.description: `requestDecided`: the request is granted or refused already, and keeps its decision. `requestLapsed`: its expiry has passed undecided. `alreadyHolds`: granting a request for a holder who holds the grant live already.

422.description: The decision is neither `granted` nor `refused`.

post.description:
Creates a grant: a role on a resource for a holder, named by subject or by address. A holder named by address is the one account in the identity provider's directory holding the address, matched exactly in any letter case, and verified; a disabled account counts. The address is never stored. A platform administrator naming the holder by address is answered `201` with the grant, and `404` `holderNotFound` when no single account holds the address. A counted owner naming the holder by address is answered `202` with a `GrantByAddress` whether or not an account holds the address, naming neither the grant nor its holder, and nothing is written when none does. An address resolving to the principal is refused as naming the principal's own subject is. A holder named by a subject the controller has never met is recorded with the grant, and answers it once signed in.

A data-plane role names a record category offered by the resource: any global category, as `global.` and its name, or one of the resource's own, as `resource.` and its name. A control-plane role, such as `owner`, names none and takes the whole resource, and an owner grant takes no expiry. A `submitter` grant naming no category takes the instance's submitter category. A grant names its record category alone: the member naming a field category, `fieldCategory`, is refused with `422`, whatever it holds, and so is `grantedBy`, since the caller is the granter. A `holder.email` that is no string, such as a list of addresses, is refused with `400`.

Who may see a resource: a platform administrator; a person holding a grant on it, an owner grant included, that is neither revoked nor expired and that they have not declined, pending or accepted; and, for a resource at the `open` or `registered` access level that is not suppressed, every signed-in principal. A retired resource is seen only by a platform administrator asking for it, and every grant operation answers it as one that does not exist. A principal who may not see a resource is answered exactly as for one that does not exist; one who may see it and holds no authority for what they ask is refused with `403` `noAuthorityOnResource`.

A resource's owners grant any role on it, `owner` included. An owner is a person holding an owner grant on it that is neither revoked nor expired and that they have accepted. A platform administrator grants the `submitter` and `owner` roles on any resource and makes anyone but themself an owner. No one grants the administrator role, `admin`.

The rules are judged in this order: the body's shape, refused with `400`; the body's own rules, `422`; whether the instance defines the role, and whether the role names a category, `422`; a platform administrator naming themself an owner, `403` `administratorSelfOwnership`; a principal naming themself, `422`, the text naming `/admin/grants/self`; a platform administrator granting any role but `submitter` and `owner`, `403` `administratorGrantsNoConsumerAccess`, answered alike whether or not the resource exists; whether the principal may see the resource, `404`, and holds authority on it, `403`; and the category, `422`. A holder named by address is looked up only once all of these pass; an address resolving to the principal is then refused as the principal's own subject is, and a grant held already is judged last, `409`.

The holder answers the grant through its decisions. When the instance accepts grants at creation, the controller records the holder's acceptance with the grant, showing the capabilities the grant's role confers then. A grant on the same terms that has expired does not stop the holder from being granted those terms again.

403.description: `noAuthorityOnResource`: the principal may see the resource and holds no authority to grant on it. `administratorGrantsNoConsumerAccess`: a platform administrator grants access that is the owners' to grant, answered alike whether or not the resource exists. `administratorSelfOwnership`: a platform administrator names themself an owner, by subject or by an address resolving to them. `serviceAccountNotPermitted`: a service account calls. `noAdministratorYet`: Usher has no administrator yet, and refuses every operation but the first administrator's nomination, its acceptance and a nominee's listing until one accepts.

404.description: `resourceNotFound`: no resource holds the externalId, or the principal may not see the one that does. `holderNotFound`, to a platform administrator: no single account holds the address verified, whether no account holds it, the account holding it has not verified it, or several accounts hold it.

409.description: The holder already holds a grant of this role on this resource and category that is neither revoked nor expired, whether pending, accepted or declined; `alreadyHolds`.

422.description: A rule is broken. `ownerGrantsDoNotExpire` names an owner grant given an expiry. The rest carry unnamed codes: a role not defined by the instance, in its exact letter case, or the administrator role, `admin`; a category not offered by the resource; a data-plane role naming no category, but `submitter`, or a control-plane role naming one; a `fieldCategory`, whatever it holds; a `holder` naming other than exactly one person, by subject or by address; an address not in the form of an address: text before and after a single `@`, holding no whitespace, comma or control character; a `grantedBy`, whatever it holds; an expiry that is no RFC 3339 instant with an offset, or one not in the future; and the principal naming themself, by subject or by an address resolving to them, the text then naming the self-grant operation, `/admin/grants/self`.

503.description: `directoryNotConfigured`: no directory is configured, so an address cannot be resolved; no `Retry-After`, since no retry changes it. `directoryUnavailable`: a holder named by address while no directory answers. The answer's `detail` tells two cases apart: no directory is configured, so the instance resolves no addresses and no retry succeeds while its configuration stands; or the configured directory cannot answer now, and a later try may succeed. `storeUnavailable`: the policy store cannot take the operation now, because it cannot be reached or the instance's database role may only read; nothing of it is written. `outcomeUnknown`: the store did not confirm whether the change was made; read what it changes before trying again. `identityProviderUnavailable`: the identity provider's signing keys cannot be fetched to verify the access token, or the token's signing key is not among those held while the latest fetch of them has failed. `signingKeyUnconfirmed`: the access token's signing key is not among those held, and the keys were fetched too recently to fetch them again; try again once the seconds in `Retry-After` have passed.

201.description: The grant is created, for a holder named by subject, or named by address by a platform administrator. `id` is its opaque id, and `kind` is `grant`. Its holder is named by subject, with `hasAccount` true and no `email`, since no directory is read for the answer.

202.description: A counted owner named the holder by address: answered alike whether or not an account holds the address. `kind` is `grantByAddress`.

post.description:
Asks for the principal's own grant of a data-plane role on a resource, ending at an expiry in the future and within the instance's longest self-grant life of the request. The holder is always the principal, so a `holder` member is refused with `422`.

An owner of the resource, as `createGrant` defines one, is granted at once, with their acceptance showing what the role confers then, and is answered `201` with the `Grant`, `kind` `grant`. Each other owner of the resource is told of the self-grant.

A platform administrator who is not an owner of the resource asks instead, and is answered `202` with a `GrantRequest`, `kind` `grantRequest`, pending. Each owner of the resource is told of the request, and no other platform administrator is. An owner of the resource or another platform administrator decides it through `POST /admin/grant-requests/{id}/decisions`, never the platform administrator who asked; one left undecided lapses at its expiry. A request on a resource without an owner is told to nobody, and only another platform administrator can grant it.

The rules are judged in this order: the body's shape, refused with `400`; the body's own rules, `422`; a platform administrator naming the `owner` role, `403` `administratorSelfOwnership`; whether the instance defines the role, and whether it is a data-plane role, `422`; whether the principal may see the resource, `404`, and holds authority on it, `403`, as for `createGrant`: a platform administrator on any resource, an owner on their own; the category, `422`; a grant held live on the same terms, `409` `alreadyHolds`; and, for a request, one by the principal on the same terms that is pending and has not lapsed, `409` `alreadyRequested`.

201.description: An owner's self-grant is created, with its acceptance. `id` is its opaque id, and `kind` is `grant`.

202.description: A platform administrator's request is recorded, pending until another decides it. `kind` is `grantRequest`.

403.description: `noAuthorityOnResource`: the principal may see the resource and holds no authority to grant on it. `administratorSelfOwnership`: a platform administrator names the `owner` role. `serviceAccountNotPermitted`: a service account calls. `noAdministratorYet`: Usher has no administrator yet, and refuses every operation but the first administrator's nomination, its acceptance and a nominee's listing until one accepts.

404.description: No resource holds the externalId, or the principal may not see the one that does; `resourceNotFound` either way.

409.description: `alreadyHolds`: the principal already holds this grant live. `alreadyRequested`: the principal has asked for this grant already, and the request is pending and has not lapsed.

422.description: A rule is broken. `holderNotTaken`: the body names a `holder`. `controlPlaneSelfGrant`: the role is a control-plane role. `selfGrantTooLong`: the expiry is past the instance's longest self-grant life of the request. The rest carry the codes `createGrant` gives them: the administrator role, `admin`; a role not defined by the instance, in its exact letter case; a category not offered by the resource; a data-plane role naming no category, but `submitter`; and an expiry that is no RFC 3339 instant with an offset, or one not in the future.

post.summary: Creates a self-grant, or asks for one

delete.description:
Revokes a grant, whether pending, accepted, declined or expired. A platform administrator revokes any grant, a peer's self-grant included, and a resource's owners revoke any grant on it. To anyone else a grant is answered as one that does not exist, as is a grant on a retired resource.

The body is sent only with a reason. Without one, the controller records `unspecified`, a reason it alone assigns and refuses from anyone else.

A grant revoked already keeps its first revocation, and a second is refused with `doesNotHold`. A resource keeps at least one owner, so revoking its last accepted owner grant is refused with `resourceNeedsAnOwner`.

`DELETE /admin/grants/`, naming no id, is answered `404` `grantNotFound` too.

requestBody.description: The reason, sent only when one is given.

403.description: A service account calls; `serviceAccountNotPermitted`, before any lookup. `noAdministratorYet`: Usher has no administrator yet, and refuses every operation but the first administrator's nomination, its acceptance and a nominee's listing until one accepts.

404.description: The id is unknown or malformed, names a grant on a resource where the principal holds no authority for the operation, or names a grant on a retired resource; `grantNotFound` for each.

409.description: `doesNotHold`: the grant is revoked already. `resourceNeedsAnOwner`: the grant is its resource's last accepted owner grant, the text saying to add another owner first.

422.description: The reason is outside the grant revocation reasons open to a principal.

2XX.description: The grant is revoked. The answer names its holder, its resource, who revoked it and when.

patch.description:
Changes a grant's expiry, removes it with `null`, or changes its role, as a JSON Merge Patch. A principal notice names the holder.

An owner of the grant's resource, as `createGrant` defines one, changes any grant on it. When they extend a grant they hold, moving its end later or removing it, or widen it, giving it a role that confers anything its current role does not, the grant must end within the instance's longest self-grant life from the change, so it gives them no more than a self-grant could; ending it earlier or narrowing its role has no such limit. A platform administrator who is not an owner of the resource may reduce any grant, ending it earlier while still in the future or giving it a narrower role, one whose capabilities are among the current role's. They may neither extend nor widen a grant they hold, whatever its role, and are refused with `403` `selfWideningNotPermitted`; of anyone else's grants they may extend only `submitter` and `owner` grants and widen a grant only within those two roles, and any other change of theirs is refused with `403` `administratorGrantsNoConsumerAccess`. To anyone else a grant is answered as one that does not exist, as is a grant on a retired resource.

A role changes within its plane: a data-plane grant to another data-plane role, keeping its category, and a control-plane grant, such as an owner grant, to another control-plane role, keeping the whole resource. No one is given the administrator role, `admin`, and an owner grant takes no expiry. A self-grant, one its holder granted themself or asked for, keeps an expiry within the instance's longest self-grant life of its request.

A revoked grant is refused with `doesNotHold`. A grant replaced by a newer grant on its terms, once it had expired, is refused with `grantReplaced`, and the newer grant is the one to change. An expired grant that nothing replaced is live again once extended.

Widening a role confers nothing new until the holder accepts the grant again: their answers are left as they are, and a grant confers only capabilities its holder accepted.

200.description: The grant is changed, and answered as it now stands.

403.description: `administratorGrantsNoConsumerAccess`: a platform administrator who is not an owner of the grant's resource extends a grant someone else holds other than a `submitter` or an `owner` grant, or widens one beyond those two roles. `noAdministratorYet`: Usher has no administrator yet, and refuses every operation but the first administrator's nomination, its acceptance and a nominee's listing until one accepts. `selfWideningNotPermitted`: a platform administrator who is not an owner of the grant's resource extends or widens a grant they hold, whatever its role, the text saying to end it earlier, narrow its role, or ask for a self-grant instead. `serviceAccountNotPermitted`: a service account calls, before any lookup.

404.description: The id is unknown or malformed, names a grant on a resource where the principal holds no authority for the operation, or names a grant on a retired resource; `grantNotFound` for each.

409.description: `doesNotHold`: the grant is revoked. `grantReplaced`: a newer grant on its terms replaced it once it had expired, the text saying to change that grant instead. `alreadyHolds`: the holder already holds a grant of the new role on this resource and category that is neither revoked nor expired. `resourceNeedsAnOwner`: the change takes the role of its resource's last accepted owner grant away, the text saying to add another owner first.

422.description: A rule is broken. `ownerGrantsDoNotExpire`: an expiry on an owner grant. `roleInOtherPlane`: a role of the other plane, such as `owner` for a data-plane grant. `selfGrantTooLong`: a self-grant's end past the instance's longest self-grant life of its request, or the end of a grant an owner of its resource holds and extends or widens past that life from the change. `selfGrantExpiryRequired`: a self-grant's expiry removed, or a grant an owner of its resource holds and extends or widens left without one. The rest carry the codes `createGrant` gives them: an expiry that is no RFC 3339 instant with an offset, or one not in the future; a role not defined by the instance, in its exact letter case; and the administrator role, `admin`.

post.description:
Records the holder's answer to a grant, `accepted` or `rejected`, with the capabilities shown to them, which are those conferred by the grant's role as it stands. Answers are appended, and the latest is current. The grant itself is left unchanged.

Only the grant's holder answers it; anyone else receives `grantNotFound`, as does anyone for a grant on a retired resource. An owner declining their resource's last accepted owner grant is refused with `resourceNeedsAnOwner`.

409.description: `doesNotHold`: the grant is revoked or expired. `resourceNeedsAnOwner`: the answer declines a resource's last accepted owner grant, the text saying to add another owner first.

422.description: The decision is neither `accepted` nor `rejected`, or the capabilities differ from those conferred by the role.

post.description:
Imports EGO's study groups from an export, for platform administrators. The administrator is checked before the body is read, and the body may be up to 10 MiB.

A run is dry unless `apply: true` is sent beside the export. A dry run writes nothing and reports exactly what a real run on the same data then does. A real run writes all of its changes or none of them, and holds a lock that refuses a second run until it ends.

Each resource registered by a run takes the instance's configured base tier and is served by every application named in `audiences`. The prefixes that read a study's id from a policy's name, and the policies granting every study, come from the instance's configuration.

Either run answers its report to the administrator alone. The report is never written to the log stream.

Nominates Usher's first administrator, for the first user alone: a principal whose token holds the configured first-user role. The nominee is the first user themself, or a person Usher has met through the trusted identity provider, named by subject. The first user is recorded on first meeting, as a base user holding no grant. They may nominate again while no administrator has accepted, and each nomination replaces every earlier one, so only the latest may be accepted.

404.description: `nomineeNotFound`: the nominee is neither the caller nor a person Usher has met through the trusted identity provider.

The body is form-encoded and holds one `logout_token`: a current logout token issued by the configured identity provider for the instance's back-channel logout clients alone, naming a session in `sid`, a subject in `sub`, or both. post.description:
Answers an Usher token for the channel assertion's application, whatever the body carries: the anonymous visitor's for a body carrying no `credential`, or the principal's for a sign-in token verified by the identity provider's realm.

The token is a compact JWE whose protected header holds `alg` `dir`, `enc` `A256GCM` and `typ` `usher+jwt` alone, encrypted under the token subkey of the application key that verified the channel assertion. Its payload is in the highest version listed by the request and served by the controller.

The first exchange verified with a key records the key's `confirmedAt`, and the audit event `applicationKey.confirmation` records it once.

The channel assertion is checked first, so an exchange whose assertion is refused does no other work. A body member other than `credential` and `payloadVersions` is ignored.

Each instance of the controller admits an application's exchanges within a share of its own exchange connections, so one application's exchanges never take another's share, and lends past a share any connection its exchanges in flight leave free. An exchange its channel assertion and its body admit, the anonymous one included, takes a place once its credential is judged; once the instance's exchanges in flight number as many as its exchange connections, one over its share, but for one anonymous exchange per application, is answered `503 admissionShareExceeded` at once, with `Retry-After`, recording nothing. An exchange admitted is answered only once its `token.exchange` audit event has been recorded, whether it is issued a token or refused: one whose event cannot be recorded is answered `503`, and no token is issued for it. Once a refused credential's refusal is recorded, every later refusal under the same key is answered at once, alike, and counted rather than recorded, until 10 minutes pass with no such refusal or an hour passes since the recorded one. The key is the token and the reason for a token that verified, and the application and the reason for any other credential.

Every exchange is answered by the controller's deadline, measured from the request's arrival and shorter than the bridge's timeout, so the bridge always has the answer before it gives up. A step the deadline cuts short is answered as that step's failure, as the responses below say.

Every refused credential, a revoked principal's, a signed-out session's and a service account's included, receives this one answer, with the same body. The caller is authenticated by its channel assertion, so a refused credential is answered `403` here, where the Management API answers the same code with `401`.

408.description: The request arrived too late to be answered by its deadline; `requestTimeout`. The controller answers every exchange by its deadline, measured from the request's arrival, and the time the body takes to arrive counts against it: a request whose body arrives whole with too little of the deadline left to judge it and record its outcome is answered here. Nothing is judged or recorded, no token is issued, and the connection is closed.

A stream is also refused when the instance cannot record the channel assertion as used.
